newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Speads over Bunds keep narrowing for Belgian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Speads over Bunds keep narrowing for Belgian bonds.

text.p: The yield premium of Belgian linear bonds over German Bunds narrowed further in volatile trading on Thursday, and traders began to wonder just how much tighter the gap could get before a violent reaction set in.
"In my opinion the spread is already too tight, but the market doesn't seems to agree with me," one trader said.

"Everybody feels the spread is way too tight at the moment. There is no risk premium at all, and there should be some. But the trouble is the lack of liquidity. There is not enough paper around," another commented. "Foreigners are not holding Belgian paper and domestic holders aren't selling."
"But it is not as simple as that. Selling Belgian paper at these levels and buying German means generating large capital gains which are liable for tax," the trader added.

Generale Bank, which traders said bought a total of more than 30 billion francs worth of Belgian bonds on Tuesday and Wednesday, pounced again on Thursday -- but this time it was working both sides of the market.
On the previous two days Belgium's biggest bank focused mainly on buying six, seven and eight year paper. On Thursday it switched to buying 10 year and selling the very long end, traders said.
"It was a very volatile day, particularly at the long end," one trader said. "Three and 10 year paper outperformed five years."
"It was a day for the longer end of the curve to flatten and the shorter end to steepen," he added.
The benchmark 2006 OLO ended the day yielding 6.22 percent against Wednesday's 6.25, with the spread over Bunds at just 16 basis points from 17 having on several occasions during the day hit 14.
The new front month futures contract was 20 basis points up at 118.35. -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810
